quest.title: Free Verse
quest.description: Penny had a dream... Well, it wasn't all a dream.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: From the moment you asked that question, you became "dear friends."

dialogues.speaker: Nana
dialogues.text: Let's go tell Penny the good news.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Found it, found it, found it.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Those little troublemakers are competing again. Whoever catches them wins!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean, the swarms of fast-swimming blue fish are the "children" we need to bring back?

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Yes! Yes! Catch up to them and tell them:

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: "I caught you! I caught you! I caught you!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like Mr. Cat Hatter was right. They really are a bunch of mischievous kids.

dialogues.speaker: Penny
dialogues.text: You have to use your head, not your ears, to truly get what others are saying.
"The little dog laughed to see such fun, and the dish ran away with the spoon."

dialogues.speaker: Dog in a Dress
dialogues.text: Woof?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Someone's singing here. Should we say hello?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should Paimon speak louder? Hello...?
Oh.

dialogues.speaker: Cat With a Black Hat
dialogues.text: Meow, meow meow.

dialogues.speaker: Dog in a Dress
dialogues.text: Woof, woof!
Okay, alright, I got it. Greetings... friends from afar.
Welcome to... our party. Please take a seat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, she looks very shy. Did we startle her?

choices.text: Let's tone it down a bit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon got you. We'll take a... Wait, Paimon's not seeing any seats!

response.speaker: Dog in a Dress
response.text: Woof, woof.

response.speaker: Cat With a Black Hat
response.text: Meow, meow-meow-meow-meow, meow!
Oh, it's okay, Nana, it's not necessary.
Mr. Quijano is right, we don't need to follow any awful rules. We just need cookies and bones.

response.speaker: Dog in a Dress
response.text: Woof... woof-woof, woof-woof... Arwoo.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you talking to the puppy?
No, not a puppy. This is... Lady Nana.
Anyway, that's it for the pre-meal speech. Time to raise a toast!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Neither does Paimon... Guess we'll just roll with it.
To all the gears, muskets, and math books!

response.speaker: Cat With a Black Hat
response.text: Meow!

response.speaker: Dog in a Dress
response.text: Woof!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Should Paimon meow or woof along? Fine... Woof!

response.speaker: Dog in a Dress
response.text: Woof! Woof, woof! Woof!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, did Paimon woof wrong...? This hasn't felt right since the start.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can someone translate their woofs and meows, please?

response.speaker: Cat With a Black Hat
response.text: Meow, meow-meow.
Sorry, you're right. As the party host, that was my negligence. I should've introduced myself first.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Penny is my name. The furry gentleman with the black hat here is Don Quijano, a swashbuckler.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Meow.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: And this is Nana, a particularly elegant and very considerate lady.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Yip-yip, {RUBY#[D]Thanks for saying that, Sweetheart.}woo-woof. Woof {RUBY#[D]Pleased to meet you.}woof.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why are you mumbling? It's our turn to introduce ourselves! This child seems to be talking to imaginary animal friends. Shouldn't we roll with it?

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: No, Lady Nana and Mr. Quijano are not imaginary, and they can speak.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oops, she heard us.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: May I tell them a little bit about you, Lady Nana? Just a little, or they won't understand what you'll say.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Woof.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Okay! Lady Nana is from the Court of Fontaine. She has a nice surname, Le...

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: *whine*

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: I won't bring that up, then, good Nana. Sorry to hurt your feelings.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: I'll just mention the happy part. Nana's best pal is the purple-eyed Autumn.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Miss Autumn is a genuine lady. She'd change Nana's outfit many times a day.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Nana wore a different dress to sleep, meals, afternoon teas, balls, walks, and even dates, with different accessories.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Then, the purple-eyed Autumn left home. Nana wandered here with her and became friends with us.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Now, would you mind, Mr. Quijano?

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Meow, meow.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Okay, I'll also just tell them a little bit about you.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Sorry, Mr. Quijano is still wanted by the Maison Gardiennage to this day, so I can't say much at all — for your own good, of course.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Years ago, when Mr. Quijano was adventuring with his buddies... Oh, that would be Rouge and the blind man Freeman.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: They were pursued by hired hitmen to Poisson. They ran out of everything except the three goons on their tail.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: That was when Mr. Quijano charged in and saved them... What was it that you said at the time, Mr. Quijano?

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Meow-meow-meow, meow-meow meow.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Right. He said, "My fine friends, I love you with all my heart, but it's time to say goodbye. We'll meet again six feet under."

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: He thought he'd never make it, so he lunged in alone and drove all three bad guys away!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, then he must be a master of the sword!

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Hehe, you believe it now, don't you?

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Rouge once said that you have to use your head, not your ears, to truly get what others are saying.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: If you still don't get it, just close your eyes and listen with your head.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The girl's words are full of fantasies, but you don't think it would hurt to go with the flow.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Keep your eyes closed a bit longer. If you're bored, I'll sing a song for you. Mr. Quijano and Lady Nana often sing it along with me.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: "Hey, diddle diddle."

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: "The cat and the fiddle, the fish jumped over the moon."

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: "The little dog laughed to see such fun, and the dish ran away with the spoon."

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: It seems the girl has always been singing by the river with but a cat and a dog for company...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: No wonder they're so close to each other. What would they say?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You meditate on that for a while...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh, {NICKNAME}, Paimon's not feeling any different, but should we try to speak with the cat and the dog?

choices.text: Can't say I've never seen things like this before, but still...
Let us raise a glass in our minds.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Always flexible no matter how weird the situation is, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case... let us raise a glass in our heads!

choices.text: Let's be careful when we speak.

talks.objective: Try to understand what Don Quijano and Nana are saying

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Meow! Meow-meow, meowr.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What are you saying? {M#He}{F#She}'s not stupid. Don't you talk bad about {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You understood that, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, it just came to Paimon without any effort.

choices.text: That's probably because you're practically a child.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Are you calling Paimon immature?

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Woof, awoo, {RUBY#[D]It's because she listens from the heart.}woof-woof-woof.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Awoo{RUBY#[D]Hello,}, woof-woof {RUBY#[D]friends from afar.}woof.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How did you know we came from far away? Can you not only speak, but tell the future just like Mona too?

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Mrow — {RUBY#[D]"Friends from afar" is a common greeting,}meow, purr, meow-meow {RUBY#[D]friends from afar.}meow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So everything Penny said is true?

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Arw-arw-arwoo {RUBY#[D]I did use to live in the Court of Fontaine,}arwoo, woo, woof-woof-woof{RUBY#[D]such wonderful memories.}, arwoo.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: A{RUBY#[D]I suppose,}woo, my old friends are still mingling regularly at the Hotel Debord.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Heh, I would often accompany Autumn to such soirees at the Hotel, and oh, how we danced!

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: We wouldn't stop dancing, not even when the band grew tired!

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Whether or not you believe me, it is all little more than a memory for me now.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: For now, Autumn has found her calling, and I have found mine. I wish only for her happiness, from the bottom of my heart.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: And Rouge has accepted me, so in the end, I stay here by choice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's fully immersed in her memory, huh.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rouge... Penny mentioned that name. Who is he?

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: He is a graceful gentleman.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: And he is Penny's guardian, as well as our friend.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Very fun to be with.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Adept at archery, and knows a thing or two about swords. An outstanding young man.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Don't dabble in dangerous deeds, Quijano, or you'll get yourself killed.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Worry not, Nana, a gremlin once foretold that I shall not die so easily.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: The prophecy says that when at last I tire of adventuring, a respectable and adorable girl shall appear.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: And in her, I shall find my purpose for all my remaining days. And I shall dedicate all that I have and am to ensuring she never comes to harm.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: That child is Penny. But how can I best protect her?

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Were I a knight, and not a swashbuckler, I would know how. Alas, I am not.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #A knight? You have one right in front of you! {NICKNAME} is an honorary knight of the Knights of Favonius!

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Oh, my! To think I should encounter a true knight!

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Then, allow me one presumptuous request...

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: I suppose we have the same idea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Heh, although there's basically nothing we, the legendary adventurer duo, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, can't do, our time is quite valuable and carries a cost.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why don't we figure out some charging plans when we have time?

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: I'd be willing to spend all of my jewels to hire a knight, so, if you could...

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Please become friends with Penny.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Our dear Penny stands at a fork in the road. She knows not whether to grow up, or remain a child.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Her body is still growing, and she grows bigger by the day.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: She is growing mentally as well, and her heart grows more complicated by the day.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: What do a cat and a dog know of such strange human things? But it should be easy for a knight.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: We need to find a knight to be Penny's friend. Perhaps then, she can find the answers.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're very good to Penny.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: She's the best child in the world.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: No one loves her more than I do.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Please be Penny's friend! I offer you all my necklaces and satin dresses.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: You have my word, that I shall protect you with mine own life should the need arise.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: The gems from Liyue traders may be priceless, but Don Quijano's promises are more precious still.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How do I become her friend, then?

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: You will!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wants to be little Penny's friend too!

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: My dear friends, herehence, you are "friends from afar" no longer.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: From the moment you asked that question, you became "dear friends."

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: This is wonderful! So wonderful! Let us tell Penny the good news.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why, of course... Wait, no, Paimon was smart to begin with! Are you doubting Paimon's intelligence?

dialogues.speaker: Nana
dialogues.text: Penny, my dear, you shall have two new friends.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: #The legendary adventurer duo, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, are willing to be our friends.

dialogues.speaker: Penny
dialogues.text: Really? Haha, awesome! I have so many friends now!

dialogues.speaker: Nana
dialogues.text: Let's have a ceremony to commemorate this.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: The ceremony requires a speech. But alas! We lack the time to write a proper one.

dialogues.speaker: Nana
dialogues.text: Don't worry. Just keep it simple.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Very well, then I shall make this brief. Please, come forward.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should do it.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Ladies and gentlemen, I hereby declare...

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Penny, friend to the children, Don Quijano the Swashbuckler, and Lady Nana, hereby welcome Paimon and...

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Ah, just a moment. How should I introduce you two?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean Paimon's title? You can call Paimon the Best Guide in Teyvat!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And let's use Honorary Knight of the Knights of Favonius for {M#him}{F#her}, though {M#his}{F#her} other titles are awesome too.

dialogues.speaker: Penny
dialogues.text: No, no, no. That's not what Mr. Quijano is asking.

dialogues.speaker: Nana
dialogues.text: We need to know who your friends are.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Every one of us, cats and dogs, are bound together by the bonds of friendship.

dialogues.speaker: Nana
dialogues.text: A life bereft of friendship... Oh! Such a life would be too horrible. So, who are your friends?

choices.text: A deity that oversees a whole nation.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Good. Penny always brings delicious food. And so, she is also a deity. The Goddess of Biscuits and Bones.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Then, my dear friends, from now on, you shall have one more deity friend.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Good. In the name of all the bearings, cakes, and storybooks—

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: #Penny, Paimon, and {NICKNAME} are now good friends.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: You will share all your bones, biscuits, and picture books, and say "good night" to each other before you go to sleep.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Play in the mud together, scare birds together, and count stars together!

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Woohoo!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woohoo!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Woohoo!

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Now, we're all friends... But wait, the two of you haven't met the children yet.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Gosh! We almost forgot the children.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Strange. I haven't seen them all day.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: The children are our friends, too. You two should meet them.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: You're right. Please go meet the children. Let them know you are their new friends.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: They probably went somewhere far away to play. It's high time they returned. Go into the water and have a look.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Don't worry, just go underwater. You needn't fret about the children not wanting to come back. I'll sing a song to send you along.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: The children will come back to sleep in their big shells when they hear my song, so head over to the big shell and wish them sweet dreams.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Oh, deary me! Those are the only friends you have? It's okay. You have us now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You are also Paimon's best friend!

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Aha! So you are a pair of good friends. Wonderful!

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: I can see that Paimon is a truly great friend!

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Bubble bubble, Penny is singing, bubble bubble.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, the "children" Penny was talking about are fish!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hello, there. We're Penny's new friends, Paimon and {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Bubble bubble, new friends? New friends... New friends!

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Bubble bubble! Sweet dreams, new friends!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sweet dreams! Well, they seem happy. Now that we've met them, let's go to the next shell.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Bubble bubble, can't find. Bubble bubble, can't find!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hello, there. We're Penny's new friends, Paimon and {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Bubble bubble, new friends! Bubble bubble, old friends... can't find!

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Bubble bubble... Penny is singing, bubble bubble... Sleepy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They seem to have lost something. Strange... But we should be done here, so let's head over to the next shell first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's nothing here... Where are the "children"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? That's a Fatui insignia!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The "children" are gone, and there's only a Fatui insignia left inside the shell! We have to tell Penny about this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Penny, we just met the "children" underwater.

dialogues.speaker: Penny
dialogues.text: How did it go? Did you become pals?

choices.text: I would call it a friendly-enough encounter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Penny, some of them went missing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #We found this in their cradles. {NICKNAME}, if you would.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This is a Fatui insignia.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: What...!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You probably don't know this, but the Fatui are a bunch of very, very bad guys. They might have kidnapped the "children."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But don't you worry, we'll help you, since we're friends now.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Bad guys?

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Are you saying that Kerek is a bad guy?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Kerek? Who or what is that?

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Kerek oft sings with Penny. I once recommended he try his luck at the Opera Epiclese.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: He does have a nice voice.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: He would go underwater to play with the children as well.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: That's right. Kerek is a swimmer most swift. I admire him greatly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, you mean there's a Fatuus named Kerek who is Penny's friend, and who left this mark behind?

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: I think so. This belongs to Kerek. He's our pal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Maybe we misunderstood.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: What are Fatui, anyway?

choices.text: A bunch of guys who love to pull dirty deeds.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Some in the Fatui love to use others and do bad things. They've opposed us loads of times.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: So is Kerek very bad? Does he do a lot of dirty deeds?

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: I can smell scoundrels from a mile away. But Kerek had not the stench of ill-will about him.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: But if our dear friends say he may be just such a person...

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Oh! I understand. Perhaps Kerek was once bad, but has since turned over a new leaf.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: There is also the possibility... that he is both good and bad.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Oh! You are quite correct. One can be both bad and good.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Just like a person can enjoy both dainty little cakes and raw seafood.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Raw seafood... Ugh... Only the worst of the worst eat that kind of thing.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Come now, Nana. Raw seafood isn't that bad.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Wrong. I shall never touch the stuff.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, if Fatui didn't kidnap the "children," where did they go...?

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Oh, don't worry. The little troublemakers often run off on their own. They'll be back soon enough.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Penny, what's on your mind? Why are you zoning out?

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Good guys and bad guys... That sounds complicated, like math. Like, what do you get when you add one good guy and one bad guy together...?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Penny spreads her fingers and frowns in deep thought but to no avail.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: She takes out a math book and scribbles... Again, to no avail.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Hmm, I can't figure this out. I haven't gotten to this part of math yet. I'll ask Autumn when she gets back.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: You must learn from an adult like Autumn, Penny. Adults know the answers to questions like this.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: We have returned to that old question once again. Does Penny want to grow up or not?

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Yes, this is the thirty-sixth time that we've raised the issue.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: We have made a list of all the pros and cons of being an adult. Do you have the list, Quijano?

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Fret not, I have long since committed it to memory.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Con #1: Adults cannot sleep on velvet cushions, for adults are hard and sturdy creatures.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: They must sleep on boards of hardwood, so that they can keep their minds and bodies hard.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: It's awful not to be able to sleep on soft cushions.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Con #2: Adults aren't allowed to catch butterflies, though I have not the slightest idea why.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: I know. I remember how Autumn grew up. It began when she stopped stepping in puddles as she passed.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Then, she refused to go barefoot after getting out of bed. She insisted on wearing her leather shoes.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: And finally, I asked her if she'd like to go catch butterflies together one day. She refused, and picked up her textbooks and went into the study.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: That was the moment she grew up. I saw her become an adult, just like that.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: That is why I believe that being an adult means you cannot go catch butterflies.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Actually, not catching butterflies is fine. There are other plenty more fun things to do.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Oh, but it's not just these, dear. Out of all those fun things, you must choose only one.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: You can't do math when you're busy eating cookies, and it's difficult to eat cake when you're holding a musket.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: That's rough. So I can't have other stuff like bearings, bows and arrows, and pretty dresses all at the same time?

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: No, dear, you can't. You can only choose one, because humans only live once.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Not to mention, Penny, that Quijano and I will no longer be able to keep you company.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: What? You can't grow up with me? How can I be without you?

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Who's going to lick my face when I wake up, who's going to tell me bedtime stories? What am I supposed to do...?

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: My poor Penny, you know my purpose is to love and protect you. I, too, am sad that I cannot grow up with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, Paimon doesn't know why, but now she feels like crying too.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Ladies, please do not weep... If I may be earnest, I cannot bear the sight of tears.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: If I could pierce that which makes you weep, I should draw my sword this instant, but I...

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Ah! I cannot bear it! I really can't! I've got to do something!

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} Knight, let us think of a way to stem their tears! We...

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: We... Perhaps we can bring the children back, and let them sing with Penny and Nana. Surely, that would make them happy!

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Yes! That is exactly what we should do! Come! Come over here now, let's figure out how to get it done.

choices.text: Growing up is not necessarily a bad thing.
A bunch of guys who see things differently than most people.

talks.objective: Discuss the situation with Don Quijano
Discuss the situation with Don Quijano

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Dear friends, how do you feel about the idea?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We just need to find the "children" and bring them back? Err, this probably isn't going to solve the real problem...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She still has to face growing pains, eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: I know, I know... But since she cannot choose... Can't we just let her grow up later?

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Were Penny to grow up just like that, who would scratch under my chin? Who would cuddle me at night as I sleep?

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: No, no! Let us give her more time.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: As Penny's dear friend, I must put a stop to her tears this very instant, and make her smile!

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Lady Nana's purpose is to love Penny, and mine is to be Penny's knight! I must protect her from harm.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Alas! I truly am a failure. To think that Penny is crying before my very eyes! If only I were a real knight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Out of curiosity, why do you want to be a knight so badly, Quijano?

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: It is my calling, friends. Have you never been entrusted with such a noble cause?

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Rouge tasked me with this duty, and I took an oath to protect Penny.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Don Quijano is one who keeps his word! Now! There is no more time to lose. We must take action now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure. Paimon doesn't want her friends to cry, either.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Count me in.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Very well. Then it's time to get up, Children!

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Listen to me, Children! Our Penny is facing an unprecedented emotional crisis!

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: We must bring back all the missing troublemakers in order to restore her smile.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Then we shall sing together for her, and make her happy. That's what friends do, right?

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Yes! Yes! Yes!

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: #Honorable {NICKNAME}, Lady Paimon, this is embarrassing, but...

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: I, Don Quijano, am well-versed in both swords and fairy tales, and I am an ingenious gentleman. But I fear... I cannot swim.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: May I task you with the glorious mission of retrieving the troublemakers from underwater?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure, it'll be a piece of cake.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Children, help our new friends out here, and don't be naughty.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Got it, got it, got it!

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Follow us, follow us, follow us!

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: What song would you like to sing, Penny?

dialogues.speaker: Penny
dialogues.text: How about a lullaby?

dialogues.speaker: Nana
dialogues.text: Oh, I love lullabies.

dialogues.speaker: Nana
dialogues.text: *whimper* I'm so sad, Penny.

dialogues.speaker: Penny
dialogues.text: Good Nana, good girl. We can't keep crying.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Ladies, be strong.

dialogues.speaker: Penny
dialogues.text: I... feel so sad, Nana.

dialogues.speaker: Nana
dialogues.text: Don't be sad, Penny... *whimper*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back, everyone. Are all the "children" back as well?

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: #Yes. The Honorable {NICKNAME}, and Lady Paimon too, they have all returned.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: We're here, we're here, we're here.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: #I've stopped crying for a while now. Nana licked all of my tears away. Thank you, good Nana. You too, Quijano, {NICKNAME}, and Paimon.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: My pleasure, Penny. It is my calling to love you, after all.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Ah-ha! I knew it, I knew our Penny would be strong enough, and would never keep crying.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Actually, I'm not that strong. I'm still a little scared and want to cry a little...

response.speaker: "Children"
response.text: It's okay, don't be afraid! Let's sing!

response.speaker: "Children"
response.text: Let's all swim and sing, Penny!

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Great idea, my friends! Sadness and sorrow have been conquered, and so we shall raise our voices in glorious song!

response.speaker: "Children"
response.text: Come here, new friends, board the wave's back, and she will carry you.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Don't worry, friends, we'll follow you on the shore.

dialogues.speaker: Don Quijano
dialogues.text: Sing, friends!

dialogues.speaker: Penny
dialogues.text: Sing!

dialogues.speaker: Nana
dialogues.text: I will sing with you!

dialogues.speaker: Penny
dialogues.text: Swim on, fly on ♪

dialogues.speaker: Penny
dialogues.text: That's a great song. I'm not scared now. It's fine to grow up! Nothing to it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was a great swim! No effort needed on our part... Though getting shot out of the water by "Bighead" at the end was plenty spooky.

choices.text: I'd love to do it again.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Friends, seeing you all smile together makes me most happy indeed!

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: I've realized something big! I must tell Rouge about this the next time I see him.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: I'm the shadow Rouge casts, and it is my honor to accompany you, my lady.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: #Oh, and another thing, when Autumn comes back from the Court of Fontaine, I must tell her about you two, {NICKNAME}, Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you and this Autumn close, Penny?

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Autumn's very nice to me. She left Nana behind to watch over me. They're my absolute favorites!

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: I am the fragrance that Autumn left behind, and your smile is my bliss, my dear Sweetheart.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Thump!

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: Nana, did you hear that? Did something just go "thump"?

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: Yes, I heard it too. And did you notice? There is something shining in Penny's eyes.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: What is that?

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: It is the light of curiosity, which illuminates every dark corner, my dear.

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: And some glistening teardrops, making you all the more gentle.

response.speaker: Nana
response.text: You have already grown up with our blessing, my good child.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, we haven't given Penny our blessings — and she's a grownup already?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's give Penny our blessings. May... uh, you always have a good appetite!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm a traveler, so... May you always have the courage to explore the world.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Explore the world...

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: I've decided!

response.speaker: Don Quijano
response.text: What did you decide, Penny?

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: #I was going to become a grownup in the Court of Fontaine, but now I've changed my mind! I want to travel just like {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean you want to be an adventurer, Penny?

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: #Yes. {NICKNAME} and Paimon are adventurers. If I want to travel like them, I have to be an adventurer too.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If you want to be an adventurer, Penny, you have to get the Adventurers' Guild's approval first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And that is a very hard thing to do, not to mention how the life of an adventurer's pretty tough, so are you sure that's what you want?

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: It's okay, I wanna give it a try!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: In that case, I'll write a recommendation for you as your rite-of-passage gift, Penny.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You borrow pen and paper from Penny and write a simple introduction letter.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Wonderful, thank you! I love it! C'mon, I'll give everyone a gift too! Please gather 'round...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Penny skips and kisses Mr. Hat and Ms. Skirt on the forehead with a smile.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Then she kisses Paimon on the cheek before you bend over...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: As Penny kisses your forehead with joy, you can almost feel her anticipation and unease about the future.

response.speaker: Penny
response.text: Dearest, most beloved friends of mine... I'm an adult now, and I'm going to be an adventurer!

dialogues.text: "Hey, diddle diddle."
"The cat and the fiddle, the fish jumped over the moon."

dialogues.speaker: Cat With a Black Hat
dialogues.text: Meow—Meow!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sure is a unique friend, who loves talking to themselves so much. But Paimon doesn't mind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go to that big shell Penny mentioned and look for the "children."

dialogues.speaker: Singing Voice from the Shore
dialogues.text: Rock a bye, baby, on seaweed-top.

dialogues.speaker: Singing Voice from the Shore
dialogues.text: When the flow combs,

dialogues.speaker: Singing Voice from the Shore
dialogues.text: The cradle will rock.

dialogues.speaker: Singing Voice from the Shore
dialogues.text: If the stem breaks, the cradle will fall.

dialogues.speaker: Singing Voice from the Shore
dialogues.text: Yet I will catch you, cradle and all.

dialogues.speaker: Singing Voice from the Shore
dialogues.text: Baby is drowsing, cosy and fair,

dialogues.speaker: Singing Voice from the Shore
dialogues.text: I sing a lullaby, oh baby hear:

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Together, together, together, let's swim.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Don't lose it, lose it, lose it.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Ahead, ahead, ahead, you'll find the troublemakers ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These kids don't feel all that reliable... But well, they are kids. We shouldn't pin too many hopes on them...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's have a closer look around and see what happens, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Stuck and so worried, so worried we are.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Get her out, get her out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This one is certainly much larger. She must be the one.

dialogues.speaker: "Bighead"
dialogues.text: Free at last, free at last! I can sing along with everyone again!

dialogues.speaker: "Bighead"
dialogues.text: Sing together, and together we sing!

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Don't be scared, don't be scared! Penny's waiting for you to go back home.

dialogues.speaker: "Scaredy-Cat"
dialogues.text: Penny, looking for us? Home, home, let's go home quick!

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Let's go home, new friends, let's all go home. Penny's waiting for us there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Let's go look for Penny. Mr. Hat and Ms. Skirt are probably waiting for us, too.

dialogues.speaker: "Bighead"
dialogues.text: Swim on, fly on, swim, swim, fly!

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: Stuck in rocks, stuck in rocks, stuck in the rocks.

dialogues.speaker: "Children"
dialogues.text: So worried, so worried, worried are we.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems like the troublemakers are trapped among the rocks. Let's try to break the rocks and rescue them.
